title: Palworld Mounts Guide | Best Flying and Ground Mounts and How to Get Them | Palworld Guide
description: Every important mount in Palworld 1.0: early Direhowl, Helzephyr and Beakon, the fastest Jetragon and Xenolord, ground kings Necromus, Paladius and Hartalis, Frostallion, plus saddles and where to catch them.

sections.heading: Why mounts matter
sections.script: Palworld's world is huge, and the right mount changes everything. A good mount saves you hours of walking, lets you reach high places, cross water and escape danger. In this guide we go through the best mounts in Palworld one point zero, from your first ground mount, to your first flying mount, all the way to the fastest legendaries, and how to get each one. Remember one rule before we start: every mount needs its saddle before you can ride it, so always check the technology tree after a new catch.

sections.heading: Your first ground mount
sections.script: Early in the game, the mount to get is Direhowl. Its saddle is one of the first you can craft, so it is usually the first Pal you will ride. It is fast enough to make early exploration much quicker, and it is easy to find. Ride Direhowl while you are collecting resources and catching your first Pals, and you will cover far more ground than on foot. It will not stay your best mount forever, but it is the perfect start.

sections.heading: Your first flying mounts
sections.script: Flying is the biggest upgrade in Palworld, because it lets you go straight over mountains and water. A great early flying mount is Helzephyr, which most guides recommend as one of the best easy upgrades before the endgame. Later in the mid game, Beakon is a strong flyer. Beakon is also handy for the Barge Oil Rig, because that rig only has gun turrets and no anti air lasers, so you can fly straight in. Once you have a flying mount, exploring the map becomes much faster and more fun.

sections.heading: Jetragon: the speed king
sections.script: The fastest mount in Palworld one point zero is still Jetragon, with a sprint speed of around three thousand three hundred. No other mount comes close. But Jetragon got much harder to get. It moved from Mount Obsidian to the Sunreach sky islands, and it jumped from level fifty to level seventy. You will find it at Dragonmark Peak, at around minus five five three, minus one three three two. It is weak to Ice, so bring Ice Pals and plenty of strong spheres.

sections.heading: Xenolord: built for long flights
sections.script: Next to Jetragon, most rankings put Xenolord at the top of the flying mounts, and it is great for long trips. But you won't find Xenolord on the map. It is a raid boss. Collect four Xenolord Slab Fragments from Feybreak dungeons and Feybreak expeditions at the Pal Expedition Station, craft the slab, and place it on a Summoning Altar at your base. Beat the raid, and you can catch one of the best flying mounts in the game.

sections.heading: Necromus and Paladius
sections.script: For ground mounts, the legendary pair Necromus and Paladius sit at the top. Both are level sixty in one point zero, and they share the same arena in the desert, at around four four six, six eight zero, so you can only summon one at a time. Necromus is a Dark Pal and one of the fastest ground mounts, with a double jump. Paladius is Neutral and trades a little speed for a triple jump. Want raw speed? Pick Necromus. Want to climb high places? Pick Paladius.

sections.heading: Hartalis
sections.script: Hartalis is another top ground mount, and like Xenolord, it is a raid boss. Build the Summoning Altar from the Ancient Technology tree, inside a base. Craft the Hartalis slab from its four fragments, place it on the altar, and the raid begins, with a timer of about ten minutes. Bring your strongest team, because raid bosses hit hard. Some guides even rank Hartalis as the fastest ground mount, so it is worth the effort if you love racing across the map.

sections.heading: Frostallion and other legendaries
sections.script: Frostallion is a great all round mount in the endgame. In one point zero it is a level sixty legendary, up from level fifty, at a frozen lake in the Astral Mountains, at around minus three five seven, five zero eight. It is an Ice Pal, so bring Fire Pals and warm gear. Frostallion is also one of the best Cooling Pals for your base, so it does double duty. Catching legendaries is much easier with a high capture rate, so collect Lifmunk Effigies and offer them at a Statue of Power.

sections.heading: Mounts and passives
sections.script: Your mount gets even better with the right passive skills. Movement speed passives make the biggest difference for mounts, and Legend boosts several stats at once. Since you cannot add passives after catching a Pal, the way to get them is breeding. Breed two of the same species to keep the mount while you improve its skills, and keep the best child. A Jetragon or Necromus with great passives is the ultimate way to travel.

sections.heading: Saddles first
sections.script: A mount is useless without its saddle. Every rideable Pal needs its own saddle, which you unlock in the technology tree and craft at a workbench. So the moment you catch a new mount, open the technology menu and check its saddle. Early saddles like Direhowl's are cheap, while legendary saddles need much higher levels and rare materials. Plan ahead and save your points and materials for the mount you really want, so you can ride it as soon as you catch it.

sections.heading: Flying in Sunreach
sections.script: Sunreach makes a flying mount essential. The region is a group of sky islands, and the only way to move between them is to fly. Unlock the Watchtowers as you go, so you can fast travel and avoid long flights. Jetragon lives there too, as a level seventy Alpha at Dragonmark Peak, so a good flyer helps you reach it. If your mount runs out of stamina over the void, you will fall, so watch your stamina bar and land on islands to rest.

sections.heading: Mounts that also work
sections.script: Some mounts are also great at your base. Jetragon has level eight Gathering, the best in the game, so on a day you are not flying it can harvest your fields. Frostallion has level seven Cooling, which keeps your food fresh. Kingpaca is a huge ground mount that also gathers at your base. Picking mounts that also work means one Pal can do two jobs, which saves space in your Palbox and in your base.

sections.heading: How to catch your dream mount
sections.script: Legendary mounts are hard to catch, so prepare. Weaken them first, because the lower their health, the better your chances. Throw from behind when you can. Craft the best spheres you have unlocked and bring a lot of them. And raise your capture rate by collecting Lifmunk Effigies and offering them at a Statue of Power. Bring Pals with the right element: Ice for Jetragon, Fire for Frostallion, and Dragon Pals against Dark ones like Necromus.

sections.heading: Which mount when
sections.script: Here is a simple roadmap. Start with Direhowl. Get Helzephyr as your first flyer, then Beakon in the mid game. In the late game, catch Necromus or Paladius for the ground and Frostallion as an all rounder. And in the endgame, go for Jetragon in Sunreach, and raid for Xenolord and Hartalis. Every step makes the world feel smaller and faster, and every new mount opens up more of the map.

sections.heading: What do you ride
sections.script: So those are the best mounts in Palworld one point zero, from Direhowl to Jetragon. What is your favourite mount, and which one are you hunting next?
